title: The Rainbow Maker
clue: A fine mist, the sun behind you, and a dark background. Everything else comes down to timing.
reveal: With the sun behind you and a fine mist in front, a small rainbow appears against a dark fence or hedge. Your dog can sniff the cool mist, stay on a dry mat or just watch you. It is your own pop-up rainbow.
objective: Make a rainbow in a garden mist, let your dog explore the spray or watch from a mat, and photograph the arc.
instructions: Pick a sunny morning or late afternoon when the sun is low, and a spot with a dark backdrop such as a fence, hedge or shaded wall. Bring a hose with a fine mist nozzle, or a spray bottle. Put a dry mat with water out for your dog.
Stand with the sun behind your shoulder and spray a fine mist ahead of you, toward the dark background. Move the nozzle until a rainbow arc shows.
Bring your dog on a leash to the mat. Keep the spray away from their face and ears, and never aim it at them.
Let your dog decide: sniffing the wet grass, walking through the cool edge of the mist, or watching from the mat all count.
Stop the spray the moment they back off. Wipe the mist from their coat with a towel if they got wet.
Take a photo of the rainbow with your dog in the frame, even if they are just standing nearby.
Finish with a cool drink and a rest in the shade.
twist: You make the rainbow yourself in the mist, and your dog is invited to walk in it, sniff it or ignore it.
completion: A rainbow has appeared, even a small one, and your dog has seen, sniffed or ignored it.
photoIdea: The rainbow arc with your dog sitting or standing at the edge of the frame.
memoryPrompt: How big was the rainbow, and did your dog watch the mist or the grass?
supplies: Hose with a mist nozzle or a spray bottle
safety: Never spray the dog's face or ears; they can walk in or out of the mist as they choose.
Run the hose first so the water is not warm from sitting in the sun.
Skip it on cold or windy days, and dry them with a towel if they got wet.
